observations: Industrial overlock sewing machine mounted on a white table stand.
The brand 'KECIL' is printed on the top of the machine head in photo 0.
Four red thread tension dials are visible on the front of the machine.
A red electronic control panel is visible on the right side of the machine head, suggesting a direct-drive motor.
The machine is threaded with four spools of white thread.
A metal stand with foot pedals is visible beneath the table.
Cardboard boxes are visible in the background, one showing a 'CE' mark.

claims.evidence: The machine appears clean and is near boxes, but there is no proof of zero usage or factory seals.
The brand KECIL is visible in photo 0, but the model number on the red identification plate is not legible.
Four tension dials are clearly visible on the machine head in photo 0.
The physical design and table mount are consistent with an industrial overlock machine (locally referred to as a weaving machine).

risks.risk: Electronic control panel or integrated motor failure
risks.proof: A video showing the machine powered on and the needle bar moving via the foot pedal.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical timing or looper issues
risks.proof: A video of the machine sewing a continuous overlock stitch on a piece of fabric.

risks.risk: Actual condition is used rather than brand new
risks.proof: A photo of the underside of the machine head and the oil reservoir to check for residue.

proof_requests: A clear, close-up photo of the red identification plate to confirm the model number.
A video of the machine powered on and sewing through a piece of fabric.
A photo of the motor and power specifications located under the table.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a KECIL brand industrial overlocker. Although the specific model number is not legible, the visible features (4-thread, direct-drive panel) allow it to be priced as a used unit in the worst case.
